Did I close the service bay door?” Sometimes I’ll turn around to check, and it’s always fine, but even on nights I don’t go back, I’ll lie there replaying it over and over in my head. Same at home with the stove, the front door, the garage—tiny things, but they stick.

Since the divorce, I’ve been thinking a lot—maybe too much—about what I did wrong, deals I might have messed up, conversations I should’ve handled differently. It’s like my brain gets hooked on one thought and just circles it. I wouldn’t say I’m completely down all the time, I still get through my day, talk to customers, crack jokes. But when things get quiet, especially at night, it’s like there’s this mental loop: “Did I screw that up? Did I forget something important?” I try to dismiss it, but it keeps coming back and wears me out.
D016-D013_h022.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D016-D013_h022.answer: A & C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D016-D013_h023.question:
It’s been a few months now where I can’t shake this constant worry that there’s something seriously wrong with my body. I work nights in the ER, so I see a lot of really sick people, and then I’ll notice, say, a random chest flutter or a headache and my mind just locks onto it. I’ll start thinking, “What if this is something we missed? What if it’s something rare?” and then I can’t let it go for hours.

Even when I’m off shift, I find myself replaying symptoms in my head, almost like I’m mentally checking myself over and over. I know it probably sounds irrational, but in the moment it feels very real. I’ll go down these mental rabbit holes about what disease I might have, and it’s hard to pull myself out. Sometimes my mood drops when I’m stuck in those thoughts, but I’m not sure which comes first—the worry or feeling low. I haven’t really changed my routine much, I still go to work and see friends occasionally, but I feel distracted and preoccupied a lot of the time.
D016-D013_h023.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D016-D013_h023.answer: A & C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D016-D013_h024.question:
It’s been a few months now where I can’t shake this idea that something is seriously wrong with my body. After so many years as a nurse, I know how things can be missed, and lately every twinge or bit of fatigue makes me wonder if I’ve got some sort of cancer or a heart problem that no one has picked up yet. I keep going over my old lab results in my head, replaying every appointment, thinking, “What if they overlooked something?”  

I find myself lying awake at night, just running through the same worries over and over. I’ll start by thinking about a little ache, and then I’m down the rabbit hole, imagining worst‑case scenarios, trying to remember every symptom I’ve ever had. Sometimes it feels tied to how low I’m feeling since my husband died; other times it just pops up on its own and won’t let go.  

It’s not like I’m doing anything strange or ritualistic, but mentally I just circle the same thoughts. I know it’s not normal to dwell like this, but I can’t seem to switch it off.
D016-D013_h024.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D016-D013_h024.answer: A & C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D016-D013_h025.question:
I’ve been… stuck in my head a lot, especially over the last few months. It’s hard to say exactly when it started, but it’s been long enough that I notice it every day now.  

At work on the psych ward, I’ll be handing meds or checking restraints and suddenly I get these flashes in my mind—like images of me hurting a patient, or doing something wildly inappropriate sexually, or mocking someone’s beliefs. They feel completely opposite to who I am, and they really scare me. I don’t actually want to do any of it, but the fact that I even think it makes me feel like a terrible person, especially given my job.  

When that happens, I tend to replay it over and over afterward, almost arguing with myself about what it means—did I secretly want it, am I dangerous, am I just failing as a nurse and as a mother? I can go over the same scenario for ages, even when I’m home alone after my kids are asleep.  

My mood has been up and down. Some days I just feel numb and exhausted, other days I function fine, but the thoughts and the mental replaying keep circling back no matter how I feel.
D016-D013_h025.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D016-D013_h025.answer: A & C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder
